How does the finance industry use cyber threat intelligence?

Financial sector is the most targeted sector for cybercrime globally — banking trojans, ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), card skimming, crypto theft. Threat intel use cases: 1) Fraud intelligence: monitor dark web markets for stolen card data, account credentials, and bank login credentials from the institution. Feed into fraud detection rules. 2) Vulnerability management prioritization: CVEs actively exploited against financial sector peers — prioritize patching over generic CVSS score. 3) Third-party risk: monitor supply chain vendors for breaches or compromise. Security ratings (SecurityScorecard, BitSight) for continuous monitoring. 4) Phishing/brand abuse: monitor for lookalike domains, fraudulent mobile apps, phishing kits targeting customers. Domain monitoring, certificate transparency alerts. 5) Regulatory compliance: SWIFT CSP requires threat intelligence sharing. FFIEC guidance on threat intel programs. FS-ISAC (Financial Services ISAC) for sector-specific threat sharing. 6) Incident enrichment: when SOC gets an alert, threat intel enrichment — is this IP/hash/domain known malicious? Attributed to which threat actor? Part of an active campaign? 7) ATM/POS: specific intel on physical skimmer campaigns, jackpotting malware (ATMitch, Ploutus).
